subject: Computing

unit.unitOverview:
Welcome to Unit 1 of Year 1 Computing at Ehel Academy. This is the very first unit of our youngest year, and it is called “Computers are everywhere.” It is a warm, gentle start — no test, no reading task, and no computer needed in the room. It is about noticing something wonderful: computers are all around us, and you already use them every day.

There are four big ideas, taken one at a time. First, computers are everywhere, and come in different shapes and sizes — a big desktop, a laptop that folds up, a flat tablet you touch, and a small smartphone. Second, we use computers for lots of different jobs — for fun, to make things, to talk to people far away, and to find things out. Third, computers use programs (also called apps), and different programs do different jobs. Fourth, we put things into a computer using input devices like a mouse, a keyboard, a microphone and a camera.
learningPath: Preview the goals, key words and the tools you will use
Read the concept explainers and study the code examples
Follow the methods and worked examples
Build the activities, debug your work and play the games
Apply, explain and finish the Unit Project and Challenge

provenance.transformation: Structured from the Cambridge Primary Computing 0672 — Stage 1 Teacher & Parent Guide, Activity Sheet and Mini-Project. Teacher-directed prose was rewritten into learner-facing explainers so the unit teaches with no adult present.

outcomes: Know that computers are everywhere — all around us, at home, at school and out in the world.
Recognise different types of computers — desktop, laptop, tablet and smartphone — and say which are big and which are small and easy to carry.
Know that we use computers for different things: for fun, to make things, to talk or message, and to find out things.
Know that computers use programs (also called apps), and that different programs do different jobs.
Know about input devices (mouse, keyboard, microphone, camera) and that we use them to put data — numbers, words, pictures, sounds and video — into a computer.

concepts.title: Computers are everywhere
concepts.explanation:
A computer is a clever machine that helps us do things. Computers are all around us — at home, at school, in the shop, in the car, even in a watch. We use them every single day.

What is this? Yes! And here is a secret — this is a computer.
concepts.example: A computer is a clever machine that helps us. Today we are going to find computers all around us!
concepts.checkYourself: Can you understand that a phone or a tablet is a computer, not only the big machine on a desk? Can you point to computers around you?

concepts.title: Different kinds of computers
concepts.explanation:
Computers come in different shapes and sizes. A desktop is big and stays on a desk. A laptop folds up like a book, so you can carry it. A tablet is flat and you touch it with your finger. A smartphone is small and fits in your pocket. Some computers are big, and some are small and easy to carry.

This big one stays on the desk — a desktop. This one folds up and you carry it — a laptop.
concepts.example: This flat one you touch with your finger — a tablet. And this tiny one fits in your pocket — a smartphone.
concepts.checkYourself: Can you name at least two of the four types?

concepts.title: What do we use computers for?
concepts.explanation:
We use computers for lots of different jobs. For fun — we play games, listen to music and watch videos. To make things — we draw and paint pictures. To talk or message — we video-call and chat with family and friends. To find out things — we search for answers about anything we wonder about.

What do you like to do on a phone or a tablet? Playing a game — that is for fun!
concepts.example: Drawing a picture — that is to make things! Calling your uncle — that is to talk!
concepts.checkYourself: Can you see that one computer can do many different jobs? Can you name at least two things we use computers for?

concepts.title: Programs and apps
concepts.explanation:
A computer uses programs to do all those different jobs. Another name for a program is an app. A program tells the computer what to do. Different programs do different jobs — one program to draw, one to play a game, one to watch videos, one to make a video call.

Each of these little pictures is an app — and an app is a program. This one plays games. This one lets us draw. Different programs do different jobs.
concepts.example: An app is a program. A program tells the computer what to do.
concepts.checkYourself: Can you understand that different programs do different jobs — a drawing app draws, a game app plays a game?

concepts.title: Putting things in: input devices
concepts.explanation:
We put things into a computer using input devices. A mouse points and chooses things on the screen. A keyboard types letters and numbers. A microphone hears your voice. A camera takes pictures and video. The things we put in — numbers, words, pictures, sounds and video — are called data.

How do I tell the computer the letter A? With the keyboard! How does it hear me sing? With the microphone! How does it take my photo? With the camera!
concepts.example: How do I point at the screen? With the mouse!
concepts.checkYourself: Can you understand that input devices are how we put things into a computer? Can you name at least one input device and say what it does?

esafety.title: Check before you trust
esafety.text: Anyone can put anything on the internet, so not everything you read is true. Check an important fact on a second, different website, and ask an adult you trust if you are not sure.

esafety.title: Tell someone if something worries you
esafety.text: If anything online upsets you, or someone asks you for personal information or to keep a secret, stop, leave the page and tell an adult you trust straight away. It is never your fault.

esafety.title: Respect other people's work
esafety.text: Pictures, music and writing belong to whoever made them. Use work that is free to use, and say where you got it. Your own work belongs to you — put your name on it.

project.title: My Computer Scrapbook
project.brief: Bring together everything from Computers Are Everywhere into one finished piece of work you can show and explain.
steps: Plan first: write down what your computers are everywhere project has to do before you build anything.
Build the smallest version that does one of those things, and run it.
Add one feature at a time, testing after each one.
When something breaks, change one thing, run it again, and note what fixed it.
Check your work against every success criterion below before you call it finished.
successCriteria: I drew or found all four kinds of computer.
I can point to each one and say its name.
I found computers around me on my hunt.
I showed my favourite app and said its job.

selfAssessment: I can know that computers are everywhere — all around us, at home, at school and out in the world.
I can recognise different types of computers — desktop, laptop, tablet and smartphone — and say which are big and which are small and easy to carry.
I can know that we use computers for different things: for fun, to make things, to talk or message, and to find out things.
I can know that computers use programs (also called apps), and that different programs do different jobs.
I can know about input devices (mouse, keyboard, microphone, camera) and that we use them to put data — numbers, words, pictures, sounds and video — into a computer.
